plan: This is structurally a second-price auction: my sealed bid acts as my maximum willingness to pay, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (the clock price when the second-to-last bidder exits). In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $34.

Since the auction mechanism functions like a second-price auction (the clock ends when only one bidder remains, and the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid), truthful bidding is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value of $28 ensures I win whenever profitable (value > competitors' bids) and never overpay, since the price I'd pay is determined by others' bids, not my own. This maximizes expected profit.

Since this auction functions as a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, determined by when others exit), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value of $14. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the market price, and I never overpay since I'll only pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit.
